partners.diseaseBName: ectodermal dysplasia 17 with or without limb malformations
partners.mechanism_chain: MESP2 (HGNC:17958) —DISRUPTS→ Notochord Development (GO:0007477); LEF1 (HGNC:6704) —DISRUPTS→ Notochord Development (GO:0007477); Notochord Development (GO:0007477) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal Malformations (HP:0002711); MESP2 (HGNC:17958) —LEADS_TO→ Spondylocostal Dysostosis (MONDO:0012097); LEF1 (HGNC:6704) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal Dysplasia with Limb Malformations (MONDO:0979228). Both MESP2 and LEF1 are crucial transcription factors involved in embryonic development. Mutations in MESP2 cause spondylocostal dysostosis, a severe disorder of vertebral and rib development, by disrupting notochord formation. LEF1 plays a role in ectodermal development and limb patterning. Loss-of-function mutations in LEF1 can lead to ectodermal dysplasia with or without limb malformations. This hypothesis posits that disruption of the shared pathway of notochord development, influenced by both MESP2 and LEF1, underlies the skeletal phenotypes observed in both conditions.
